claims.statement: Under the no-zero-sum-of-length-at-most-seven and at-most-two-terms-per-cyclic-subgroup hypotheses of BSP2012 Lemma5.2, replacing a pair x,2x with x,x cannot create a new short zero sum; iterating removes all x,2x pairs.
claims.notes: The two terms x and 2x fill the cyclic subgroup's two allowed slots. Replace 2x by x. Any new zero sum with zero or one of the two x copies yields the same original zero sum; if it contains both, replace them by the single original 2x to yield a strictly shorter original zero sum. Therefore absence of sums of length at most seven is preserved; support shrinks and iteration terminates. This proves ONLY the first printed without-loss reduction, not later classification steps, Lemma5.2, eta7 or the exact k-wise coefficient.

claims.statement: In BSP2012 Lemma5.2's p7 no-short-zero-sum context after eliminating x,2x pairs, if two distinct cyclic subgroups each contain two different occupied values, a GL2(F7) change of basis normalizes their four values to (1,0),(3,0),(0,1),(0,3); this does NOT establish that two such subgroups are impossible.
claims.notes: On each mixed line the ratio of the different occupied values is not 2 or 4 by prior CLM-0076 reduction, not 6 by absence of short length-2 zero sums, leaving 3/5 which become ratio3 on swapping. Distinct lines give independent basis. Conditional normalization only; at-most-one-mixed-line classification and eta7 still unverified.

claims.statement: Conditional on BSP2012 Lemma5.2's terminal p7 reduction providing at least two copies each of (1,0),(0,1),(t,t), values t=0,3,5,6 each force a nonempty zero sum of length <=7, but this does not establish the preceding reduction or exclude t=1,2,4.
claims.notes: Explicit forbidden subsums: t0 singleton zero; t3 2(3,3)+(1,0)+(0,1)=(7,7), length4; t5 (5,5)+2(1,0)+2(0,1)=(7,7), length5; t6 (6,6)+(1,0)+(0,1)=(7,7), length3. All hypotheses are conditional on prior multiplicity existence; no whole-lemma or eta upgrade.

This excludes ONLY this conditional multiplicity-two branch.
claims.notes: Coordinate sets S0={0,3,4,6}, S1={1,2,5,6}, S2={0,1,3,4}; allowable eight vectors (2,3),(2,4),(3,2),(3,5),(4,2),(4,5),(5,3),(5,4). Nine remaining indexed terms force duplication. Does NOT establish at-most-one mixed line, (5,5) zero/one copy branch, downstream classification, eta7 or printed Lem2.3 coefficient.

claims.statement: Under actual BSP2012 Lem5.2 p7 15-term no nonempty zero sum of length <=7 and capacity-two-per-cyclic-line hypotheses, following CLM-0081, at least six cyclic lines each have two identical nonzero indexed terms; there must be three distinct doubly occurring x,y,z with x+y in <z>. Pure GL2 geometry proves the alternative six-line pair sums confined to the other two lines is impossible.
claims.notes: COMPLETE hand proof ONLY of doubled-triple existence geometry. Seven lines full, one singleton; at most one mixed line leaves six equal-doubled lines. If pair sums avoid those six lines they lie on two complementary lines, sent to axes. Fix v1=(r,s), five other selected vectors fall in two coordinate-opposition classes, each at most two because three would force impossible pairwise opposite nonzero coordinates in odd characteristic. Subsequent forbidden doubled (1,0),(0,1),(2,2), normalizations, t1/2/4, full Lem5.2 and eta7 remain UNPROVED.
